A PHOTOGRAPHER’S FIELD NOTES

What does your
day feel like?

An intimate gathering

At a wedding at home, the doorway can matter as much as the ceremony. Tell us who will be waiting there and which corners of the house hold a memory for you.

A ceremony rooted in tradition

Two families can celebrate the same ritual in different ways. Walk us through yours, especially the fleeting gestures and the people you want in the frame.

A weekend away

A welcome dinner, a sangeet, a quiet breakfast together. When the people you love travel to one place, decide which moments around the ceremony belong in your photographs too.

03 / THE LENSQUEEN WAY

Be in the moment.
We’ll keep it.

Wedding photography and cinematography with a love for honest emotion, beautiful light, and the people who make your story yours.

01 Your story first +

Tell us about the two of you, your celebrations, and the moments that matter most. Every story starts with a conversation.

02 Space to be yourselves +

From the anticipation to the celebrations, make room for laughter, connection, and everything that happens naturally.

03 Made to be relived +

Photographs to return to. Films to feel again. A way to carry the atmosphere of your day into the years ahead.

Before you enquire.

What should we send in our first message?

Start with your date, venue or city, and the functions you have in mind. If a detail is still undecided, tell us what you know so far.

How do we plan our family portraits?

Write down the groups you want together and choose someone who knows both families to gather them. Flag anyone who needs a seat or will be leaving early.

What if we feel awkward in front of a camera?

Tell us what puts you at ease. A walk together or a few minutes away from the crowd can be a comfortable starting point for portraits.
